answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table (compliance), circuit breakers and read-replica routing don't address write-path latency on the primary, and adding capacity mid-peak is slower and uncertain if the new release introduced a write-path regression. Regional failover matches the observed signature (degradation confined to primary region) and memory_b2 indicates it restored latency quickly before. Key risk to flag: failing over during peak settlement writes carries a write-loss window, so the failover must be executed with write-drain/replication-lag checks to satisfy the no-lost-writes objective; if lag is too high, add_capacity becomes the fallback. Verifying b2 (failover efficacy) and b3 (capacity as fallback) before committing.
